content:
emma: FYI a couple of user reports about our JS SDK pulling undici into client bundles and failing on older Node. They show up after upgrading to 1.4.0.

ryan: Do we know why undici is ending up in browser builds? Our package.json uses conditional exports, right?

emma: We do, but consumers using certain bundler configs (vite older versions, CRA) still resolve import('undici') during static analysis because of some transpiled interop. Example error: 'Uncaught SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module' in the browser console.

theo: Common root cause: static imports or top-level await usage that forces bundlers to include the Node-only path. We should ensure all Node-specific code uses dynamic import and never reference undici from the main entry.

priya: Also saw a Node <18 repro where TypeScript compiled down to CJS and users expected fetch but it's not present. They end up doing `npm i undici` and then bundler picks that up for client too. We need better docs for CJS fallback.

emma: Proposal: add a small runtime adapter inside the SDK and ship it as the only public entry. It will dynamically resolve to one of three providers: global fetch, undici (dynamic import), or cross-fetch (only when user explicitly wants legacy browser polyfill).

ryan: Adapter sketch:
```js
// getFetchAdapter.js
export async function getFetchAdapter() {
  if (typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function') return globalThis.fetch;
  // dynamic import prevents static bundlers from including undici
  const { fetch } = await import('undici');
  return fetch;
}
```
Note: keep this file in ESM and referenced only by async paths.

priya: For CJS consumers we need a tiny shim: `module.exports = require('./dist/interop-cjs').default` that lazily imports the ESM runtime. That avoids forcing users to move to ESM immediately.

theo: Important: docs must show how to exclude undici from browser bundles. Quick examples: webpack config alias `{ undici: false }` or `resolve.alias` to a noop module; Vite: `ssr.noExternal: ['undici']` is opposite, we actually want `optimizeDeps.exclude: ['undici']` and `build.rollupOptions.external` when doing SSR builds. Add specific examples.

emma: Typings: a lot of confusion in support tickets about fetch types in Node. Recommend adding a TypeScript note: suggest `tsconfig.json` snippet: `{"compilerOptions": { "lib": ["ES2021", "DOM"] }}` and mention the downside (DOM lib pulls in many DOM types). Also provide a minimal `types/fetch.d.ts` that declares the fetch signature for server-only projects.

ryan: Tests we should add: 1) bundler build that simulates client bundle (esbuild/vite) and assert undici not present; 2) Node <18 runtime test with undici fallback; 3) Next.js Edge function smoke test.

priya: One UX note: when SDK lazy-loads undici, network call latency may add a tiny cold-start. We should document that and optionally allow customers to call `await ensureFetch()` at app startup to warm it. Provide example: `if (!globalThis.fetch) ensureFetch()` in server entry.

theo: Also add telemetry: if we detect we had to load undici, emit a debug log so we can measure how many users rely on fallback. Keep logs opt-in / debug only.

infra-bot: CI job triggered: run/ci/sdk-bundling-check on branch fetch-adapter-2026 (started).

emma: I'll draft the doc, include the webpack/Vite/rollup snippets, CJS shim, and the ensureFetch pattern. Will open PR and tag @ryan @priya for review.

ryan: Great. Also add a short FAQ: "Why does my browser bundle include undici?" with checklist to debug (check imports, bundler config, package exports resolution).

priya: I can add the TS minimal types and a tiny npm package example for CJS.

emma: Thanks team. Plan: land docs + SDK adapter next sprint and add the three tests.
